data: 14 UTC days x 5000 unique one-sample series/day; same stock unmodified O1, identical v11 RAW UUID SAMPLES day-partitioned for all variants; no synthetic customer/private data.
intervention: SQL per-series avg_then_group_avg + SAMPLES id IN and JOIN held structurally same; metadata source is original TAGS Map extraction vs extra day-partitioned cover with pre-extracted String labels. This tests combined day-partition/label materialization/access path, NOT partitioning alone.
comparator: Same runner ABBA TAGS/cover/cover/TAGS; 2 warmups+4 measured each of four phases, 4 cases, 64 measured 32 warmups, exact native PromQL output oracle on every trial, no RSS OOM, all control drifts <=25%.
interpretation: Standalone sidecar speeds selective stage1d 1.48x and broad3d 1.72x relative to same-shape original-TAGS SQL, but broad1d regresses 19% and broad14d regresses 4%.

Crucial falsification: 14d sidecar does NOT improve same-shape SQL, though SQL with sidecar was ~2.97x faster than native PromQL in a DIFFERENT run. Thus the prior native-vs-SQL gain cannot be attributed to the sidecar; query rewrite/column projection/operator DAG is a major candidate. Do NOT multiply ratios across runners.
Read rows fall 150k->30k for broad1d while wall worsens; reducing read rows alone is not enough. Broad14d read rows unchanged 210k each, and sidecar is slower.
No native planner integration, late-write atomic revision, ACL, dense/multi-point long-lived, continuous ingest, replica or peak process RSS proof.
next_gate: Same-runner full-native PromQL vs original TAGS-based SQL ABBA without sidecar, with identical source and PromQL output oracle. This isolates SQL rewrite gain without new metadata structure; only then consider source patch or specialized SQL option. Preserve negative 1d broad and 14d sidecar findings.
